findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 3, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. Both JSON commands reach this `git hash-object` call once for every story with a plan read, so git calls grow as read stories accumulate. Stories with both local and remote branches also trigger a per-story `git merge-base` in `story.py:548`. The cache removes repeated reads of the same story but does not bound calls across stories, leaving the Done-when call bound unmet on a normal growing repo.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Gate. This switches `forge next --json` from fresh PR lists to lists cached for 60 seconds. If a teammate merges a PR after the cache is filled, the command can still treat it as open and offer the previous next step. Forge's own PR writes invalidate the cache, but an external merge does not. That changes the observable JSON despite the recorded allowance promising the same JSON.
findings.title: Allowance mismatch: forge next --json can use stale pull request state

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test. The named call-count proof adds stories without `.read.md` files and deletes their local branches at line 41. It therefore never exercises the per-story `git hash-object` and `git merge-base` paths, and passes while those calls grow with ordinary read stories and locally checked-out stories. Its output assertion at line 56 also checks only the added fixes.
